findings.description: Critical: Spec Authorized and Observable Ingestion and design D6 require cross-lane rate-limit writes when the principal has `report_vendor_rate_limit` or a trust-level 3 administrative override. `report_vendor_rate_limit` is not in `ADMIN_ACTIONS` / `TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS`, so `authorize_operation` falls through to the profile allowlist only. A trust-3 principal without `vendor_limit_reporter` is denied for cross-lane POSTs; API tests mock `authorize_operation` and never assert the trust-3 override.

findings.description: Critical: Design D10 requires durable coordinator audit for coordinator-side observation lifecycle. `VendorRegistryService._audit_event` only calls `audit.log_operation` when `self._audit is not None`, but `get_vendor_registry()` and the watchdog factory construct `VendorRegistryService()` / `VendorRegistryService(db=...)` with `audit=None`. Production therefore emits only `logger.info`, unlike other coordinator services that wire `get_audit_service()`.

Critical: Spec Missing or ambiguous catalog row requires that a non-unique configured join leave cost unknown and that the miss be audited without heuristics. `_cost_projection` drops zero-match models silently and only `logger.warning`s ambiguous matches—no durable audit and no explicit miss marker in the projection payload—so partial joins can still yield `cost.known=True` while omitted models disappear.

Critical: Task 4.4 and design D7 require reporting provider-dispatch capacity failures once per result. `PhaseDispatchResult` carries additive `agent_id` / capacity fields and tests only assert field propagation, but `dispatch_phase` / `normalize_dispatch_result` never call `report_vendor_limit_result` (or any bridge writer), so autopilot capacity outcomes are never persisted.

Critical: Spec One model limits before fallback succeeds and D7 require per-attempt model-scoped reports. `ReviewOrchestrator` assigns `sdk_adapter._capacity_callback = report_vendor_limit_result`, but `SdkVendorAdapter.dispatch` catches `_SdkCapacityError` and `continue`s without invoking the callback. A successful SDK fallback after model A capacity leaves no model-scoped observation.

Critical: Sync CLI capacity callbacks report model-scoped limits, then `_collect` always re-reports terminal `CAPACITY` via `report_vendor_limit_result`. Final `ReviewResult` omits `capacity_scope`/`capacity_model`, so the reporter defaults to lane scope. For a single-model (or last-model) exhaustion this marks the whole lane limited after an already-recorded model-scoped observation, contradicting D4 model-scope semantics.

Critical: `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch_async` treats model capacity with `continue` and returns terminal `CAPACITY` without `_notify_capacity` / `capacity_callback`. Intermediate model-scoped limits are lost on the async submit path even though the sync CLI path notifies at the matching capacity branches.

Critical: Design D8 requires preserving selected lane identity through selection into subsequent retry context (`to_agent_id` / `dispatch_agent_id`). After a switch decision, `_execute_item_phases` rebuilds `context` as only `{item_id, roadmap_id, completed_items}` and continues; `to_agent_id` is recorded in provenance but never injected into the next `dispatch_fn` call, so exact-lane routing remains prompt-layer optional.

Nit: Design D7/D8 name the structured lane field `dispatch_agent_id`, and roadmap policy reads `dispatch_metadata.get("dispatch_agent_id")`. `phase_agent` / `provider_dispatch` only add optional `agent_id`. Callers that forward the phase payload field name as-authored never satisfy the orchestrator's exact-lane seam without an adapter rename.

Nit: When `dispatch_agent_id` is present, policy provenance sets `durable_persistence: "reported_by_dispatcher"` without invoking the reporter. Presence of a lane id is not evidence an observation was written, so D7/D10 audit consumers can over-read persistence success.

Optional: D8 requires continuing under availability policy with `cost_guard=unavailable` and a warning when a USD ceiling cannot be evaluated. Legacy `_evaluate_switch` logs that warning; `select_registry_lane` (the orchestrator path) sets `cost_guard` but does not warn when `cost_ceiling_usd` is set and the exact quote is missing.

Nit: Runtime returns `application/problem+json` with `type=urn:vendor-registry:invalid-observation` for invalid POSTs, but OpenAPI `Problem.type` enum only lists unknown-lane / unavailable / observation-conflict. `400` responses are not schema-bound to `Problem`, so this is contract drift rather than a hard route violation.

findings.description: none: GET/POST vendor routes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`; source principal is server-derived on POST; own-lane writes skip cross-lane auth while cross-lane writes require `report_vendor_rate_limit`; 404/409/503 use RFC7807 problem types matching the contract; observation_id/reason/reset/model/metadata bounds (including max 20 metadata keys) are enforced in `VendorRateLimitObservationRequest`.

none: Registry reads batch one probe query, one active-limit query, and one `model_catalog` read; SQL RPCs implement atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction; replay hashes absolute reset / retry-after / default-TTL markers without receipt time; `now >= stale_after/reset_at` expires state; tables contain no price columns; quotes use decimal arithmetic with explicit `ROUND_HALF_UP` at six places as recorded in `choices.json`.

none: Bundled `agents.yaml` declares explicit `location` / `policy_vendor` / `catalog_vendor`; lane identity maps `agent_id=name`, `vendor_type=type` without inferring location from suffixes; catalog joins use exact model ID plus optional endpoint_kind/base_url/catalog_vendor constraints with no fuzzy publisher heuristics, supporting multi-publisher lanes when IDs collide by yielding unknown rather than guessing.

none: Watchdog persists every lane snapshot on the first poll with `stale_after = observed_at + 2×VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` and skips transition events; `no_probe_method` maps to `unknown`; per-lane persist failures are isolated; compaction runs from `run_once`; Dockerfile copies `vendor_health.py` and sets `SKILLS_ROOT`/`AGENTS_YAML`; `start_notification_runtime` starts watchdog independently of notification channels.

none: `vendor_limit_reporter` refuses provider-to-lane inference and never masks dispatch failures; sync CLI fires model-scoped callbacks before successful fallback; bridge helpers preserve distinct `coordinator_unavailable` / `server_error` / `malformed_response` / `unknown_vendor_lane` errors without returning an empty successful registry.

none: Roadmap policy obtains lanes from `try_list_vendors` (no embedded `claude/codex/...` discovery roster); registry outage fail-closes unless an explicit `agents_yaml_fallback` is injected with unknown availability/cost only; exact `dispatch_agent_id` excludes only that lane while legacy provider-only signals exclude matching `policy_vendor` for the current decision; `quote_lane_cost` requires model+tokens and six-decimal ROUND_HALF_UP; static tiers rank candidates but do not populate or enforce USD in `select_registry_lane`.
